## The Core Issue

The relevant issue is [#11916 "Improve error recovery for strings and f-strings"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/11916). The problem is that there's more to f-strings than a normal string literal because it can contain an expression element. This means that there could be an unterminated f-string or the closing curly brace could be missing or an error in the expression itself.

At the time, the parser drops all unterminated strings—or more precisely, the lexer doesn't emit the string token for unterminated strings. This is for both normal and formatted string literals.

The specific f-string/unclosed brace scenario you're asking about: there's a NonLogicalNewline token after a variable because of an unclosed {. This would require a modified re-lexing logic to (1) recover from an unclosed { and (2) recover from an unterminated f-string. This also requires moving the error handling from the lexer to the parser.

## The Re-Lexing PR (#11845)

The main implementation is [PR #11845 "Implement re-lexing logic for better error recovery"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/11845) by dhruvmanila. This PR implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing.

Some technical details from the PR discussion:
- The logic reduces the nesting level by 1. It shouldn't reset it to 0 because otherwise the recovery from nested list parsing will be incorrect.
- On maintaining context: In this case, the parser should recover from the unclosed [, but the parser and lexer should remain in a parenthesized context because of the (.

There was also a design discussion about the return type of the re-lexing function. One reviewer asked what's your reasoning for returning a bool over the re-lexed kind of the token? The author responded that initially it was kept as Option<TokenKind> but the current usage doesn't really require the token itself. There's no other particular reason to use bool apart from that.

## Broader Context

This work fits into a larger tracking issue, [#10653 "Error recovery improvements for the new parser"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/10653), which tracks any improvements that could or should be made when working on error recovery for the new parser.

The re-lexing work stems from Ruff's move to a hand-written recursive descent parser (v0.4.0), where a key goal was complete error recovery: ensure that the parser recovers from all syntax errors, providing developers with an uninterrupted experience in the editor.

## The core PR: Implementing re-lexing logic (#11845)

The main pull request that introduced re-lexing was **PR #11845 by dhruvmanila**. This PR implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing.

A key design detail in that PR relates to **nesting levels**: It then reduces the nesting level by 1. It shouldn't reset it to 0 because otherwise the recovery from nested list parsing will be incorrect.

There was also a design discussion in the PR about the API of the re-lexing function. A reviewer asked what's your reasoning for returning a bool over the re-lexed kind of the token? dhruvmanila responded that initially he kept it as Option<TokenKind> but the current usage doesn't really require the token itself, and there's no other particular reason to use bool apart from that.

## The `re_lex_logical_token` snapshot and f-string nesting problem

The specific snapshot test file you mentioned (`re_lex_logical_token.py.snap`) surfaced a subtle nesting bug tied to how parentheses interact with re-lexing: when the lexer emitted the `)` token, it reduced the nesting level by 1 and the re-lexing also reduces the nesting level by 1 making it 0, which means there'll be a Newline token after `c` which is incorrect. The proposed fix was that we could check if the current token would reduce the nesting level in re-lexing logic and avoid reducing it again.

## The f-string connection (#11871 and #11916)

The f-string handling was more difficult. In **PR #11871 ("Use re-lexing for normal list parsing")**, dhruvmanila noted the tension between lexer and parser errors: for f-strings both the lexer and parser could add an error, and if the lexer adds an error it'll emit an Unknown token — suggesting they might want to move the unterminated f-string error into the parser.

This was tracked more fully in **Issue #11916 ("Improve error recovery for strings and f-strings")**. That issue explains why f-strings need a *modified* re-lexing approach: there's more to f-strings than a normal string literal because it can contain an expression element, which means there could be an unterminated f-string, a missing closing curly brace, or an error in the expression itself. The problem manifests as a NonLogicalNewline token appearing after a variable because of an unclosed `{` — requiring a modified re-lexing logic to (1) recover from an unclosed `{` and (2) recover from an unterminated f-string. It also required moving the error handling from the lexer to the parser.

## Later refinement (#20848)

More recently, the f-string recovery was improved further in **PR #20848 by MichaReiser**, which improves the lexer to preserve STRING tokens instead of converting them to Unknown if a string literal misses its closing quotes, setting a flag on the string literal instead. However, preserving the kind for unclosed string literals regressed the f-string's and t-string's recovery mechanism, so that was improved too, including preserving the F-STRING middle even if it's unclosed and better recovery for a missing `}`.

**Title:** Avoid consuming trailing whitespace during re-lexing

**Merge commit SHA:** `cdc7c7144997ca9aa99a6bfae9dd73b4fa53de49`

**Body:**

## Summary

This PR updates the re-lexing logic to avoid consuming the trailing whitespace and move the lexer explicitly to the last newline character encountered while moving backwards.

Consider the following code snippet as taken from the test case highlighted with whitespace (`.`) and newline (`
`) characters:
```py
# There are trailing whitespace before the newline character but those whitespaces are
# part of the comment token
f"""hello {x # comment....

#                     ^
y = 1

```

The parser is at `y` when it's trying to recover from an unclosed `{`, so it calls into the re-lexing logic which tries to move the lexer back to the end of the previous line. But, as it consumed all whitespaces it moved the lexer to the location marked by `^` in the above code snippet. But, those whitespaces are part of the comment token. This means that the range for the two tokens were overlapping which introduced the panic.

Note that this is only a bug when there's a comment with a trailing whitespace otherwise it's fine to move the lexer to the whitespace character. This is because the lexer would just skip the whitespace otherwise. Nevertheless, this PR updates the logic to move it explicitly to the newline character in all cases.

fixes: #11929

## Test Plan

Add test cases and update the snapshot. Make sure that it doesn't panic on the code snippet in the linked issue.
